__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Select your existing Prometheus datasource on import.

panels.title: Alerts received by outcome (per hour)
panels.description: duplicate climbing while accepted stays flat is the healthy shape for a flapping alert -- Alertmanager re-sends a firing group every group_interval until it resolves, and dedup is what stops that from being a fresh diagnosis every five minutes. The two rising together means dedup is broken and the model budget is draining.

panels.title: Diagnoses by outcome (per hour)
panels.description: incomplete is the loop's only failure that raises nothing -- MAX_ITERATIONS exhausted without reaching submit_diagnosis, still returned as a Diagnosis. blocked is a guardrail refusing before any model call; failed is an upstream breaking. Collapsing any of these into one counter hides which one a rising line actually means.

panels.title: Diagnosis duration p50/p95 (s)
panels.description: A diagnosis is six to ten model calls, not one -- buckets reach 600s for that reason. The tail is the interesting number: a p95 running close to the ceiling is indistinguishable from one that is merely slow until you check whether MAX_ITERATIONS was the reason it stopped.

panels.title: Guardrail blocks by guard (per hour)
panels.description: The label is the whole signal. 'the agent refused something' is not actionable; guard="breaker" means something is broken and one more action will not fix it, guard="namespace" means the model aimed at the wrong cluster, guard="llm_calls" means the hourly model budget is spent. Every refusal in guardrails.py leaves through one function, so nothing refuses without landing here.

panels.title: Proposal lifecycle by state (per hour)
panels.description: proposed vs executed is the ratio this service is judged on: how much the agent wanted to do against how much a human let it. blocked and failed are deliberately separate lines -- one is a working guardrail refusing a second time at click time, the other is the cluster write itself breaking.

panels.title: Model retries by status (per hour)
panels.description: Evidence the Day 20 retry works at all, not just that it exists. A line that never moves is a retry nobody has proven fires; one that climbs constantly against a single status is a provider outage to escalate, not a transient blip to absorb quietly.

panels.title: Diagnosis completion rate (%)
panels.description: Share of diagnoses that reached submit_diagnosis rather than exhausting MAX_ITERATIONS. Raised from 6 to 10 on Day 17 evidence that six turns was not enough headroom for gather-plus-one-retry; a falling number here is the same symptom returning.

panels.title: Approval rate (%)
panels.description: executed over proposed, 24h. Deliberately uncolored: a low number is not failure and a high one is not automatically trust earned, since a rejection is the guardrails working as designed. This is the number worth watching over weeks, not reacting to in the moment.

panels.title: Alert suppression rate (%)
panels.description: Share of arriving alerts that were the same fingerprint seen within SHA_ALERT_DEDUP_TTL. Also uncolored -- a rising number during an incident is dedup doing its job on a flapping alert, not a fault.
